title: An infinite payout that's worth about $30
description:
Flip a fair coin: the pot starts at $2 and doubles on every tails, and the first heads pays you the pot. Half the time you win $2, a quarter of the time $4, and so on, so every round adds $1 to the average payout and the average is infinite. But the infinity lives in pots nobody can pay: a bank of about a billion dollars can only cover the first 30 rounds, so against a billionaire the game is worth about $30, and against a bank as big as the world economy (about $84 trillion) still under $50. Nicolaus Bernoulli posed it in 1713; Daniel Bernoulli's 1738 paper in St. Petersburg gave it its name.

Numbers checked in code (every average, the capped banks, and a million simulated games). Source: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Petersburg_paradox

facts_checked: Rules: pot starts at $2, doubles each tails, first heads ends the game and pays the pot; expected value 1 + 1 + 1 + ... = infinite (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Petersburg_paradox)
Nicolas Bernoulli posed it in a letter to Montmort, 9 September 1713; Daniel Bernoulli's 1738 paper in the Commentaries of the Imperial Academy of Science of Saint Petersburg (Wikipedia)
"Few of us would pay even $25 to enter such a game" (Ian Hacking, quoted by Robert Martin; Wikipedia)
Every round adds $1: (1/2^k) x 2^k = 1 for all k (verify.py)
1 game in 32 pays more than $32; round 30 pays 2^30 = $1,073,741,824 (verify.py)

Finite banks (Wikipedia's table): billionaire $1,075,000,000 -> $30; millionaire $1,050,000 -> $20; world GDP 2020 $83.8 trillion -> $46. With a bank of exactly $1 billion and the capped tail included: $30.86; world GDP with the tail $47.19, under $50 (verify.py)
1,000,000 simulated games: about 50% pay $2, about 3.1% pay more than $32 (verify.py)
CTA: millionaire's game is worth about $20 (20 full rounds; $20.91 with the capped tail, verify.py)

beats.say: Its average payout is infinite. It's worth about 30 dollars.
No trick coin. Nicolaus Bernoulli wrote this game down in 1713.
The pot starts at 2 dollars. Every tails doubles it. The first heads ends the game, and you take the pot.
Half the time you win 2: a dollar on average. A quarter of the time, 4: another dollar. Every round adds a dollar, forever.
So pay any price? Almost nobody would pay even 25 dollars. They're right.
Play it a million times. Half your games pay 2 dollars. Only 1 game in 32 pays more than 32.
The infinity hides in giant pots. By round 30, the pot passes a billion dollars.
And who pays you? A billionaire covers only those first 30 rounds. A dollar each: about 30 dollars.
Even the whole world's economy makes it worth under 50. The infinity was never on the table.
So if a millionaire runs the game, what's your fair price?
